summary: r3 FINAL (revised after r2 reviews: optimistic APPROVE, pessimistic NEEDS_REVISION with 1 MAJOR + 1 MODERATE + 1 MINOR, all small). Replace run_optimize's MOCK bench (fixed 1000ns, correctness_fn=None — a pre-existing M2.3 gap) with a REAL GpuTimestamp MIN-of-N bench + a variant-vs-variant differential + bench_variant's tri-state device-keyed CPU oracle, all by reusing existing machinery (zero compiler/codegen/runtime change). Plus the cheap polish bundle: M3.22 PW-1, M3.19a/b/c. r3 fixes: (1) MAJOR reference-attribution blind spot — the differential is now a DETECTOR not an attributor; an unattributable divergence (no registered oracle) ERRORS the run via OptimizeError::VariantsDiverge with ZERO artifacts (refuse to crown anyone), direction-independent, closing the r2 hole where a garbage variant-0 could reject the correct majority and win; AT-3017 rewritten + AT-3017b reverse leg added. (2) MODERATE NaN-collapse — differential_mismatch gets a BITWISE blob-equality fast-path FIRST (bit-equal->match), only bit-inequal falls to the f32-ULP compare, so two distinct garbage NaN-patterns can't false-match. (3) MINOR — AT-3015 is an in-crate #[cfg(test)] test in optimize.rs so cross_validate stays PRIVATE (in-module-visible); the r2 pub(crate) promotion is dropped. Everything else from r2 stands (both reviewers verified).

differential_mandate: DETECTOR, NOT ATTRIBUTOR (r3 MAJOR fix to r2's overclaim). RATIONALE: for the common unoracled case (only saxpy/vector_add/q4_0 registered), r1's 'proceed on NotChecked' let a fast-but-wrong variant (dropped barrier / race — often FASTER) win silently. All @strategy variants are the SAME kernel with different perf knobs, so on identical SEED=0 input they must produce identical output; correctness_fn already reads back each variant, so a disagreement is a real signal. BUT the reference is just the FIRST variant's readback, NOT ground truth — so the differential can only DETECT disagreement, it CANNOT ATTRIBUTE it. r2's bug: it rejected the LATER (non-reference) variant on mismatch, silently presuming ordinal-0 is correct; if ordinal-0 is the garbage variant, r2 rejects the correct majority and crowns the garbage — WORSE than blanket-proceed. MECHANISM (r3): first passing variant seeds a RefCell reference + reference_ord (memory: one copy, few KB); each later variant compared by differential_mismatch (BITWISE fast-path then f32-ULP within ulp_tol — absorbs legit reduction-order rounding, catches gross divergence); a mismatch is RECORDED into a `divergence` ordinal set, NOT rejected on the differential alone. ATTRIBUTION comes ONLY from a registered oracle: check_correctness Ok/Failed sets oracle_attributed=true and a Failed variant is rejected on ground truth. DECISION in run_optimize after grid_search, before any write: (a) divergence empty -> proceed (fastest wins); (b) divergence non-empty AND oracle_attributed -> oracle handled it, proceed with survivors; (c) divergence non-empty AND !oracle_attributed -> Err(OptimizeError::VariantsDiverge{ordinals,kernel}), ZERO artifacts — refuse to crown anyone (attribution impossible). DIRECTION-INDEPENDENT: fires the same whether the garbage variant seeded the reference (ordinal 0) or diverged from it (AT-3017 non-reference ordinal + AT-3017b reverse leg at ordinal 0). NotChecked (case a) now honestly means 'variants agreed with each other but no absolute oracle confirmed the shared answer'. LIMITATION: non-f32 output buffers use an f32 reinterpretation for the fall-through leg (bitwise fast-path is exact; binding_plan carries element type for a future refinement; registered oracles + M3.22 fixtures are all f32/u32-copy).
push_constant_timing_disclosure: r2 (pessimistic MAJOR): zero-filled push constants can measure a NO-OP degenerate kernel for scalar-gated kernels (e.g. `if pc.n==0 { return }` or `for k in 0..pc.K`), so a variant can 'win' by doing nothing — its timing/winner is not meaningful. Scalars CANNOT be blindly random-filled (random u32 loop-bound ~4e9 -> hang/OOB) — that is why zero-fill exists; the honest fix is DISCLOSURE, not seeding. Only cheap reuse available: buffer-length-derived n (bench_variant.rs:474/492 'we use buffer length as n here') — but that is oracle-local (baked into registered CPU references), not a general size-coupled-scalar satisfier. So: documented limitation until a future axc optimize --push-constants surface.
